bromo.tagline: One epic sunrise. Five smoking volcanoes. Zero hiking experience required.

highlights.title: 5 volcanoes, 1 view
highlights.body: Bromo, Batok, Kursi, Watangan and Widodaren all sit inside one crater, with Java's highest volcano, Semeru, smoking quietly in the background.

highlights.title: Higher than Bromo itself
highlights.body: Your sunrise viewpoint sits at roughly 2,770 m, about 440 m above Bromo's own summit. You'll be looking down into the crater you're about to walk into.

highlights.title: A sacred sunrise
highlights.body: Local Tenggerese legend says a prince sacrificed everything to save his kingdom here. Locals still throw offerings into the crater every year at Yadnya Kasada.

stats.label: Summit altitude
stats.note: Chilly alpine air and views above the clouds

stats.label: Sunrise viewpoint
stats.note: About 440 m above Bromo's own summit

stats.label: Sea of Sand
stats.note: A vast, ancient caldera with a moon-like landscape

stats.label: Pre-dawn temperature
stats.note: Summit wind gets cold before sunrise

packing.why: Heavy jacket or windbreaker, beanie and gloves. Summit wind gets cold before sunrise.
A buff or mask protects your lungs from fine volcanic ash.
Standard athletic shoes work great. Heavy mountaineering boots are not required.
It's pitch dark for most of the walk. Cold air drains batteries fast, so keep a power bank ready.

assessment.title: The jeep does the heavy lifting
assessment.body: No technical climbing or heavy gear. A 4x4 jeep carries you almost all the way to the top viewpoints.

assessment.title: Flat sand, then stairs
assessment.body: From the jeep park it's flat sand, then concrete steps with handrails up to the crater rim. Pace yourself.

assessment.title: Chilly morning air
assessment.body: Pre-dawn temperatures drop to about 5°C. Staying warm and waking up at 2 AM are your biggest obstacles.

semeru.tagline: Java's highest volcano, with a lake camp and a savanna on the way up.

highlights.title: The roof of Java
highlights.body: Mahameru, the summit of Semeru, stands at 3,676 m. It is the highest point on Java and the top of the island's highest active volcano.

highlights.title: Ranu Kumbolo lake camp
highlights.body: A mountain lake inside Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park, about 4 hours' walk from Ranu Pani. Nights here are cold and frost is common.

highlights.title: Oro-oro Ombo savanna
highlights.body: After the lake the trail crosses Oro-oro Ombo, a wide savanna that fills with purple verbena flowers in season.

stats.label: Summit temperature
stats.note: Expect frost at camp and freezing air on top

packing.why: Summit temperatures reach -5°C and frost is common at Ranu Kumbolo at night.
The final climb from Arcopodo is loose sand and scree that fills your boots.
Ranu Kumbolo lake water must be treated before you drink it.
The summit push starts in the dark, in the coldest hours of the night.

assessment.title: The summit push is the crux
assessment.body: From Arcopodo the path is a 45° slope of loose sand and scree. Most hikers leave camp around 2 AM. Falls and rockfall are the main risks here.

assessment.title: Plan your water
assessment.body: Treat water from Ranu Kumbolo. Above it, water is not reliable. Carry 4–5 L for the high camp and summit day.

assessment.title: This is an active volcano
assessment.body: Semeru can erupt and the summit crater gives off toxic gas. Check the official status before you go and turn back if told to.

arjuno.tagline: A 3,339 m peak with a high meadow camp, twinned with sulfur-steaming Welirang.

highlights.title: Twin peaks with Welirang
highlights.body: Arjuno (about 3,339 m) and Welirang (about 3,156 m) form one twin volcano complex, about 50 km south of Surabaya and 20 km north of Malang.

highlights.title: Lalijiwo plateau camp
highlights.body: Lalijiwo Plateau (Lembah Kijang) sits at 2,530 m below the summit. It is the usual camp on the Tretes route and has a water source.

highlights.title: Old stone steps on Purwosari
highlights.body: The Purwosari route passes many remains from the Majapahit era, including old stone steps and spiritual sites.

stats.label: Summit elevation
stats.note: Higher of the Arjuno-Welirang twin peaks

stats.label: Ascent time
stats.note: Most hikers camp on the way up

packing.why: Above Pos 2 the forest trail is easy to lose in fog.
Fog is common and the trail gets slippery when wet.
Nights and the summit are cold, and the ridge is exposed to wind.
Springs are found at Pos 1–2 but are unreliable above Pos 3.

assessment.title: Fog is the main danger
assessment.body: Above Pos 2 the forest path is easy to lose when fog rolls in. Stay together and check your map often.

assessment.title: Steep and long
assessment.body: Expect steep climbs and 8–10 hours up. Most people split it over two days with a night at Lalijiwo.

assessment.title: Windy summit ridge
assessment.body: The ridge near the top is open to wind and cold. Bring a warm layer even on a sunny day.

welirang.tagline: A working sulfur volcano, where miners still haul sulfur off the summit.

highlights.title: Named after sulfur
highlights.body: Welirang means sulfur in Javanese. Below the 3,156 m summit an active crater still gives off sulfur smoke.

highlights.title: Sulfur miners at work
highlights.body: Miners carry loads of sulfur, often over 100 kg, from the summit down to Pondokan by cart. From there jeeps take it down the mountain.

highlights.title: Twin of Arjuno
highlights.body: Welirang is the sulfur-bearing half of the Arjuno-Welirang twin volcano, so many hikers climb both peaks on one trip.

stats.label: Summit elevation
stats.note: Active crater just below the top

packing.why: The sulfur mining area has toxic fumes. Cover your nose and mouth and do not linger.
Dense fog is common on this mountain.
It gets cold at camp and on the summit.
Steep, rocky sections near the top are hard on knees and balance.

assessment.title: Move fast through the fumes
assessment.body: Sulfur gas near the crater and mining area is toxic. Walk through without stopping, and turn back if the wind blows it onto the trail.

assessment.title: Rocky last stretch
assessment.body: The final climb is a rocky scramble. Take it slow and keep three points of contact where it gets steep.

assessment.title: Carry your water
assessment.body: Springs are only on the lower trail. Fill up there, since there is no water near the summit.

raung.tagline: A remote volcano with a huge caldera and a knife-edge rim to the true summit.

highlights.title: A 2 km wide caldera
highlights.body: Raung is one of Java's most active volcanoes. Its summit caldera is about 2 km wide and 500 m deep, ringed by a grey rim.

highlights.title: Puncak Sejati, the true top
highlights.body: The highest point of the rim, Puncak Sejati, is reached from Kalibaru. It takes 3 long days and includes short sections of roped rock climbing.

highlights.title: Razor-thin ridge
highlights.body: The Kalibaru route crosses the narrow Sirothol Mustaqim ridge and sheer rock faces where hikers use ropes and harnesses.

stats.label: Summit elevation
stats.note: Puncak Sejati, highest point of the rim

stats.label: Water to carry
stats.note: Only reliable spring is at Pos 1

packing.why: Rockfall is a real risk on the rim and the technical sections.
The route to Puncak Sejati has short roped climbing sections.
Nights are cold and the ridge takes extreme wind.
Water is reliable only at Pos 1. Carry enough for the rest of the climb.

assessment.title: Not for beginners
assessment.body: The crater rim has 300 m+ drops on both sides and needs rope work. Go only with experienced guides and real climbing skills.

assessment.title: Two routes, two goals
assessment.body: The Sumber Wringin route from the north reaches the rim. Only the Kalibaru route goes on to Puncak Sejati, the true summit.

assessment.title: Wind and isolation
assessment.body: There is no phone signal above Pos 1. Avoid the rainy season, when wind on the rim is extreme.

argopuro.tagline: Java's longest hiking trail: days of forest, savanna and old temple ruins.

highlights.title: Longest trail in Java
highlights.body: Argopuro is known for the longest hiking route on Java. The two main routes start from Bremi and Baderan, and Baderan is gentler but longer.

highlights.title: Temple ruins on Rengganis
highlights.body: Rengganis peak (3,059 m), next to the 3,088 m Argopuro summit, holds the ruins of a Hindu temple. The rock is sulfurous and the smell is strong.

highlights.title: Danau Taman Hidup
highlights.body: Hikers on the Bremi route pass Danau Taman Hidup, a lake at about 1,980 m in the Hyang Highland Wildlife Sanctuary.

stats.label: Summit elevation
stats.note: Puncak Argopuro, highest of three peaks

stats.label: One-way traverse
stats.note: ~40 km if you return the same way

packing.why: Water near Rengganis is sulfurous and must be filtered carefully.
Forest between Pos 1 and Pos 3 is easy to get lost in, and there is no signal on the whole trail.
This is a multi-day traverse with no resupply on the trail.
Several cold nights at altitude on the plateau.

assessment.title: An endurance test
assessment.body: Plan 3–4 days on the trail. Food, water and pacing matter more than speed.

assessment.title: You are on your own
assessment.body: There is no phone signal on the entire trail. Leave your plan with someone and carry a GPS.

assessment.title: Gas near Rengganis
assessment.body: The Rengganis area has pockets of sulfurous gas. Do not camp in low hollows there.

ijen.tagline: A short pre-dawn hike to the world's largest acidic crater lake.

highlights.title: The largest acid lake
highlights.body: Kawah Ijen holds the world's largest highly acidic lake. Its turquoise water has a pH as low as 0.5, about as strong as battery acid.

highlights.title: Blue fire
highlights.body: The blue flames are sulfur gases that catch fire as they escape from cracks and meet the air. They are not blue lava.

highlights.title: Sulfur miners
highlights.body: Miners work through the night, breaking yellow sulfur off the crater floor with metal poles, often with only a wet cloth against the fumes.

stats.label: Crater elevation
stats.note: Cold before dawn, so bring a warm layer

stats.label: Round trip
stats.note: Plus about 1 km down into the crater

stats.label: Ascent time
stats.note: Wide path that gets steeper near the top

packing.why: Sulfur gas in the crater can spike suddenly when the wind shifts, and it can be lethal.
The hike starts in the dark, around 1–3 AM.
The rim is cold in the hours before sunrise.
The path into the crater is steep, rocky and slippery, with no barriers.

assessment.title: Easy to the rim
assessment.body: The path from Paltuding is about 3 km with 500 m of climbing. No technical skills are needed, but the top part is steep.

assessment.title: The crater is the risky part
assessment.body: Gas levels inside the crater can rise fast. Keep your mask on, follow ranger instructions and turn back if it gets hard to breathe.

assessment.title: Blue fire is not guaranteed
assessment.body: Since 2025 the big blue flames are rarely seen, and access to the lower crater has been limited. Go for the lake and sunrise.

penanggungan.tagline: A short climb up a sacred mountain lined with centuries-old temple sites.

highlights.title: Over 130 old sites
highlights.body: In 2013 a Ubaya survey team counted 131 archaeological sites here: temples, bathing places, cave hermitages, walls and old roads.

highlights.title: A sacred mountain
highlights.body: Known as Pawitra, the mountain has been sacred since the 10th century and was a spiritual heartland of the Majapahit empire.

highlights.title: Close to Surabaya
highlights.body: At 1,653 m, Penanggungan sits about 50 km south of Surabaya, so it works as a day trip from the city.

stats.label: Summit elevation
stats.note: A small peak with a big history

stats.label: Water to carry
stats.note: Little shade on the upper trail

packing.why: The trail gets slippery in the wet season.
The upper section has little shade.
Springs are only near the lower pos, so carry your own.
The rocky section near the summit has loose stones.

assessment.title: A good first real climb
assessment.body: The trail is short and has phone signal at most points. The hardest part is the loose, rocky stretch near the top.

assessment.title: Heat, not cold
assessment.body: The upper trail is open and hot. Start early and carry enough water.

assessment.title: Respect the ruins
assessment.body: Many old sites are along or near the trail. Do not climb on them, move stones or leave rubbish.

panderman.tagline: A short, steep climb above Batu with wide views of Arjuno and Welirang.

highlights.title: A beginner's mountain
highlights.body: Panderman rises above Kota Batu, with its main peak Basundara at 2,045 m. It is known as a good climb for beginners and weekend hikers.

highlights.title: Views from Basundara
highlights.body: From Puncak Basundara you can see Kota Batu, Gunung Arjuno, Gunung Welirang and Gunung Banyak.

highlights.title: Camp at Latar Ombo
highlights.body: The trail climbs through pine forest to Latar Ombo, a clearing about 2–3 hours up where many hikers rest or pitch tents.

stats.label: Ascent time
stats.note: Steepest part is the final push

packing.why: Carry your own water for the climb.
Open sections get strong sun. Start early to avoid the heat.
The summit can be windy and cold.
Mountain weather changes fast and the trail is slippery when wet.

assessment.title: Short but steep
assessment.body: The last 30 minutes from Watu Gede to the summit are very steep. Use your hands and go slowly.

assessment.title: Go early
assessment.body: Start in the early morning to beat the sun on open sections and reach the top while the sky is clear.

assessment.title: Slippery after rain
assessment.body: The trail turns slippery when wet. Avoid the heavy-rain months of December to February.

butak.tagline: The high point of the Kawi massif, crowned by a wide summit savanna.

highlights.title: Wide summit savanna
highlights.body: Near the summit a broad savanna opens up where the Panderman route ends. It is roomy enough for camping.

highlights.title: Four ways up
highlights.body: Routes start from Gunung Panderman, Batu, the Sirah Kencong tea estate in Blitar, and Desa Wonosari. Wonosari is the longest.

highlights.title: Top of the Kawi massif
highlights.body: At 2,868 m, Butak is the higher of the Kawi-Butak twin stratovolcanoes, on the border of Malang and Blitar.

stats.label: Summit elevation
stats.note: Highest point of the Kawi-Butak massif

stats.label: Round trip
stats.note: Long traverse with no easy way down

stats.label: Ascent time
stats.note: Most hikers camp on the savanna

stats.label: Water to carry
stats.note: No water on the Sirah Kencong route

packing.why: The ridge is exposed to wind and weather, with no shelter.
Water is limited, and the Sirah Kencong route has none at all.
Nights on the open savanna are cold.
Long traverse days and pre-dawn starts for sunrise.

assessment.title: Exposed ridge
assessment.body: The ridge between Panderman and Butak has no shelter from wind or lightning. Turn back if storms build.

assessment.title: Dry season only
assessment.body: Climb between May and September. In rain the ridge becomes too dangerous.

assessment.title: Water depends on route
assessment.body: Carry all your water on the Sirah Kencong route. On the Panderman route, ask at basecamp about water on the savanna.

kawi.tagline: A quiet forest climb on the body of the 'sleeping princess' beside Butak.

highlights.title: Twin of Butak
highlights.body: Kawi (2,551 m) and its higher neighbour Butak (2,868 m) form the Kawi-Butak twin stratovolcano complex in East Java.

highlights.title: The sleeping princess
highlights.body: Seen from afar, the massif looks like a sleeping woman: Kawi forms the body and Butak the head on the west side.

stats.label: Round trip
stats.note: A long day or one night out

packing.why: The forest trail is poorly marked and easy to lose.
The summit approach is steep and slippery, worse when wet.
The summit is cold and windy.
Springs are only lower down and are unreliable above Pos 2.

assessment.title: Navigation is the challenge
assessment.body: Trail markers are few in the forest. Go with someone who knows the route, and track your position.

assessment.title: Steep, slippery top
assessment.body: The final approach to the summit is steep. Take extra care after rain.

assessment.title: Check fire status first
assessment.body: Large fires hit the Kawi-Butak massif in 2026. Confirm the route is open before you plan a trip.

anjasmoro.tagline: A forested range of about 40 peaks, protected as a conservation area.

highlights.title: About 40 peaks
highlights.body: The Anjasmoro range has about 40 peaks and spreads across Jombang, Kediri, Mojokerto, Malang and Batu.

highlights.title: A protected forest
highlights.body: Anjasmoro sits inside Tahura Raden Soerjo, a conservation forest set up to protect its plants, animals and water catchment.

stats.label: Highest point
stats.note: Tallest of about 40 peaks in the range

stats.label: Peaks in the range
stats.note: Spread over five regencies and cities

assessment.title: Few trail markers
assessment.body: Trails have few clear markers, push through deep wet brush, and cross steep, rugged ground. Getting lost is a real risk.

wilis.tagline: A dormant volcano range with coffee farms low down and misty forest above.

highlights.title: Sleeping volcano
highlights.body: Wilis has not erupted in historic times, but hot springs and warm ground water show there is still heat below.

highlights.title: Coffee farms and fog
highlights.body: On the Kare route, the first post is a coffee plantation. Thin fog often covers the slopes in the morning.

highlights.title: A road in history
highlights.body: General Sudirman crossed the Wilis area during the independence war, before the battle of 11 March 1949.

stats.label: Ascent time
stats.note: Plus 4-5 h to come back down

stats.label: Round trip
stats.note: Depends on the route you pick

stats.label: Water to carry
stats.note: Springs only low down; carry your own higher up

packing.why: Several peaks sit on one ridge and fog rolls in. It is easy to head for the wrong top.
Springs are only at lower elevations. Carry your own for the upper sections.
Nights on the ridge get cold, especially if you camp.
Dense fog and damp forest will soak you, even outside the rainy season.

assessment.title: Navigation is the challenge
assessment.body: The range has many peaks. On the ridge between them, in fog, you need a track to follow and should check it often.

assessment.title: Quiet trails
assessment.body: Few people hike here. Tell someone your route. Phone signal fades at lower elevations and is gone near the top.

assessment.title: Moderate but long
assessment.body: Some sections are steep. Plan 5-7 hours up and 4-5 hours down.

liman.tagline: The highest point of the Wilis range, reached by long, quiet forest trails.

highlights.title: Top of the Wilis range
highlights.body: Liman, also called Trogati or Ngliman, is the highest peak of the Wilis range at 2,563 m.

highlights.title: Where five paths meet
highlights.body: The name is said to come from the Javanese 'proliman', a meeting of five paths or five areas.

highlights.title: Coffee farms to forest
highlights.body: The Kare route starts in a coffee plantation, then climbs past Bukit Teletubbies into the forest.

stats.label: Summit elevation
stats.note: Highest point of the Wilis range

stats.label: Ascent time
stats.note: Plus 5-7 h to come back down

stats.note: A long day or an overnight trip

stats.label: Water to carry
stats.note: No water higher up on the trail

packing.why: There is water low on the Wates route, but none higher up and none on the Pulosari route.
Dense forest makes the trail hard to follow, and you may meet nobody.
It is a long trail far from villages. Pack enough for the whole trip.
The trail is long. Poles save your knees on 5-7 hours of descent.

assessment.title: Long and remote
assessment.body: Plan 7-9 hours up. The area is isolated, so tell someone your route and return time.

assessment.title: Water is the limit
assessment.body: Fill up low down. Above that, you only have what you carry.

assessment.title: Forest navigation
assessment.body: Thick forest hides the path. Follow a GPS track and turn back if you lose it.

kelud.tagline: An active volcano whose crater was reshaped by the 2014 eruption.

highlights.title: Where 'lahar' comes from
highlights.body: The 1919 eruption killed about 5,000 people, mostly by hot mudflows. After it, 'lahar' became the world's term for a volcanic mudflow.

highlights.title: A dome made and lost
highlights.body: In 2007 a lava dome filled the crater. The 13 February 2014 eruption destroyed it and threw ash as far as West Java, about 500 km away.

highlights.title: Tunnels against floods
highlights.body: After the 1966 eruption, the Ampera tunnels were cut to lower the crater lake and cut the lahar risk.

stats.label: Summit elevation
stats.note: Low, but one of Java's most dangerous volcanoes

packing.why: Volcanic gas and fine dust can hang around the crater area.
There is no water on the trail. Carry all you need.
Eruption debris makes the ground loose and unstable.

assessment.title: Check the alert level
assessment.body: Kelud can erupt with little warning. Only go when PVMBG has it at Level I (Normal), and follow any crater distance limits.

assessment.title: Short but loose
assessment.body: The walk is short for a beginner, but the ground near the crater is unstable. Stay on the path.

assessment.title: No water, little shade
assessment.body: Bring all your water and start early.

lemongan.tagline: A steep, sandy volcano cone above the Ranu Klakah crater lake.

highlights.title: Lake at the trailhead
highlights.body: Ranu Klakah, at the foot of the trail, is a lake-filled maar: a crater left by a steam blast.

highlights.title: Ringed by craters
highlights.body: Up to 27 maars and about 60 small cinder and spatter cones surround the volcano.

highlights.title: Busy past
highlights.body: From 1799 to 1898 Lemongan poured out up to 15 lava flows. Its last confirmed eruption was in 1898.

stats.label: Summit elevation
stats.note: Small, but the climb is steep

stats.label: Ascent time
stats.note: Plus 2-3 h to come back down

packing.why: There is only one small water point on the mountain. Guides say bring at least two large bottles each.
The upper trail is loose sand and stone on steep slopes.
Many hikers climb at night to avoid the midday heat on the open slopes.

assessment.title: Short but steep
assessment.body: The upper slopes are steep, with loose sand and rock. Expect to use your hands in places.

assessment.title: Carry your water
assessment.body: Water on the trail is scarce. Fill up at the base and ration it.

assessment.title: Few trail markers
assessment.body: Markers are limited in the forest. Keep a GPS track handy.

pundak.tagline: A short beginner hike to a grassy ridge of Welirang, above Pacet.

highlights.title: A shoulder of Welirang
highlights.body: Pundak ('shoulder') is one of the ridges of Gunung Welirang. A small plaque and flagpole mark the top.

highlights.title: Three-mountain view
highlights.body: From the grassy top you see Penanggungan to the north, Welirang to the south and the Anjasmoro range to the west.

highlights.title: Beginner favourite
highlights.body: It is a popular first climb for beginners, especially in the school holidays.

stats.label: Round trip
stats.note: Easy to fit in a morning

packing.why: There is no water to rely on along the trail. Carry your own.
The trail is slippery in the wet season and has some steep sections.
Rain is common in the wet season, and the top is open grassland.

assessment.title: Easy, with steep bits
assessment.body: Most of the trail is gentle forest walking. A few sections are steep and get slippery after rain.

assessment.title: Good first mountain
assessment.body: It is short, close to Pacet town, and has phone signal. A good place to learn the basics.

ranti.tagline: A short, steep climb beside Ijen, with views down to the crater.

highlights.title: Next door to Ijen
highlights.body: The Ranti trailhead is about two minutes' walk from the Kawah Ijen trailhead at Paltuding.

highlights.title: Crater and cloud views
highlights.body: Hikers climb Ranti for sunrise, a sea of clouds and a view over Kawah Ijen.

highlights.title: Two tops
highlights.body: Most hikers stop at the north top (2,578 m). The true summit (2,626 m) is overgrown and hard to reach.

stats.label: Water to carry
stats.note: No confirmed water on the trail

packing.why: The trail is steeper than Ijen's and sandy. Poor shoes lead to falls.
You start from Paltuding, high on the Ijen plateau, often before sunrise.
Most people climb in the dark to reach the top for sunrise.

assessment.title: Short but steep
assessment.body: About two hours up on a steep, sandy path. Take it slow on the way down.

assessment.title: Stop at the north top
assessment.body: The true summit is overgrown and needs a machete. The north top is the usual goal.

assessment.title: Check Ijen status first
assessment.body: Ranti shares its trailhead with Ijen. If Ijen is closed for gas or fire, do not go.

merapi-ungup.tagline: The highest peak of the Ijen range, inside a strict nature reserve.

highlights.title: Crescent-moon crater
highlights.body: The summit crater is extinct. A mound in its middle is shaped like a crescent moon, which gives it the name Kawah Bulan Sabit.

highlights.title: East of Kawah Ijen
highlights.body: Merapi, also called Merapi Ungup-ungup, rises east of Kawah Ijen in the Ijen range.

stats.label: Summit elevation
stats.note: Highest point of the Ijen range

assessment.title: Not an open trail
assessment.body: The crater route is unclear, very steep and prone to landslides. It is not open to the public.

lawu.tagline: Java's sacred mountain: temples, stone stairs and cold sunrises at 3,265 m.

highlights.title: Mountain of the last king
highlights.body: Legend says Brawijaya V, the last king of Majapahit, fled to Lawu when his kingdom fell and built places for meditation there.

highlights.title: Temple start
highlights.body: The Candi Cetho route starts at a Hindu-Javanese temple. Its slopes are gentler and grassier than the stony Cemoro Sewu route.

highlights.title: Night of 1 Suro
highlights.body: On the night of 1 Suro (1 Muharram) many people climb to the top to pray and make pilgrimages.

stats.label: Summit elevation
stats.note: Hargo Dumilah, the highest of three peaks

stats.label: Ascent time
stats.note: Plus 4-5 h to come back down

stats.label: Summit cold
stats.note: Frost is possible at the top

stats.label: Main routes
stats.note: Cemoro Sewu, Cemoro Kandang, Candi Cetho

packing.why: The summit can drop to -5°C. You need a fleece, down jacket, hat and gloves.
Nights at the camps are cold, especially in the dry season.
The stone stairs above Pos 3 are steep and slippery when wet.
Most people start the summit push before dawn for sunrise.

assessment.title: Stairs above Pos 3
assessment.body: On Cemoro Sewu the trail becomes natural stone steps. They are steep and slippery when wet. Take it slow.

assessment.title: Cold and wind
assessment.body: The summit area is exposed and can reach -5°C. Cold, not the trail, is the main risk.

assessment.title: Avoid 1 Suro crowds
assessment.body: Pilgrim nights get very busy. For a quiet climb, go on a weekday in the dry season.

merbabu.tagline: Wide savanna ridges and a close-up view of Merapi at 3,145 m.

highlights.title: Savanna after Pos 3
highlights.body: Selo, the most popular route, crosses open savanna with wide views toward Merapi.

highlights.title: Merapi up close
highlights.body: From the high camps you can see Lawu to the east, Telomoyo and Ungaran to the north and Merapi to the south.

highlights.title: Five official routes
highlights.body: Hikers can choose Selo, Thekelan, Cuntel, Suwanting or Wekas. Each route crosses different landscapes.

stats.label: Summit elevation
stats.note: Cold and windy at the top

stats.label: Ascent time
stats.note: Plus 5-6 h to come back down

stats.label: Round trip
stats.note: Usually done with one night camping

packing.why: The savanna is fully exposed to wind, sun and storms.
The summit can drop to -5°C before dawn.
Springs are only near Pos 1-2. There is none on the savanna.
There is no shade on the open savanna.

assessment.title: Exposed savanna
assessment.body: Above the forest there is no cover. Wind, sun and storms hit hard. Turn back if a storm builds.

assessment.title: Steep, rocky summit
assessment.body: The final push is steep and rocky. Leave early and watch your footing in fog.

assessment.title: Fire season care
assessment.body: From August to October the grass is dry and burns easily. No open fires, and check the park's status.

merapi.tagline: Indonesia's most active volcano, climbed only when the volcano allows it.

highlights.title: Indonesia's most active volcano
highlights.body: Merapi sits on the border of Central Java and Yogyakarta and has erupted regularly since 1548.

highlights.title: The 2010 eruption zone
highlights.body: The 2010 eruption was Merapi's largest since 1872. Over 350,000 people were evacuated and the summit dome was blown apart.

highlights.title: Pasar Bubrah plateau
highlights.body: From New Selo the trail climbs to Pasar Bubrah, a bare, lunar plateau at about 2,640 m. Above it is a steep 300 m climb on loose scree to the crater.

stats.label: Summit elevation
stats.note: Height changes as the lava dome grows and collapses

stats.label: Water to carry
stats.note: No water sources on the volcanic trail

packing.why: Volcanic bombs and falling rock are real hazards on the upper slopes.
Toxic volcanic gas can collect near the summit and fumarole field.
There is no water on the trail. Carry everything you drink.
Night starts in the cold and dark are normal for a sunrise push.

assessment.title: Check status first
assessment.body: Only climb when BPPTKG says the volcano is at Level I (Normal). The summit is never guaranteed to be open.

assessment.title: Loose final climb
assessment.body: Above Pasar Bubrah the path is steep volcanic sand and scree. It is tiring and unstable, and the summit shape changes after eruptions.

assessment.title: No signal up high
assessment.body: Phone signal is patchy low down and gone above Pos 2. Tell someone your plan before you start.

sumbing.tagline: Sindoro's taller twin, with one of Java's hardest summit pushes.

highlights.title: Twin of Sindoro
highlights.body: Sumbing and Sindoro are two cone volcanoes facing each other across the Kledung Pass (about 1,400 m). Many hikers climb both.

highlights.title: One of Java's highest
highlights.body: At 3,371 m, Sumbing is one of the highest mountains in Java. It is an active stratovolcano.

highlights.title: Garung, the classic route
highlights.body: Garung is the normal route. The basecamp sits around 1,500 m and hikers must start before 12:00 because the trail is long and steep.

stats.label: Ascent time
stats.note: Long day with big elevation gain

stats.label: Water to carry
stats.note: Springs near Pos 1; unreliable above Pos 2

packing.why: Night temperatures near the summit can drop to about -5°C.
The final push is very steep, with loose soil, rock and slippery sand.
The upper ridge and summit are exposed to wind and fog.
Water above Pos 2 is unreliable. Fill up low on the mountain.

assessment.title: A long, steep day
assessment.body: Plan 8-10 hours up. From Pos 3 the path is very steep loose soil and rock, and it gets sandy and slippery near the top.

assessment.title: Real cold and wind
assessment.body: Expect temperatures down to about -5°C, strong wind and fog. Good layers matter more than speed.

assessment.title: Start early
assessment.body: Garung asks hikers to leave basecamp before 12:00. Late starts mean finishing in the dark.

sindoro.tagline: A sandy volcano cone above tea gardens, facing Sumbing across Kledung.

highlights.title: The northern twin
highlights.body: Sindoro faces its slightly taller twin, Sumbing, across the Kledung Pass. The two cones look almost alike.

highlights.title: Start in the tea gardens
highlights.body: The Tambi tea plantation, running since Dutch colonial times, covers Sindoro's lower slopes. One route climbs from Sigedang through it.

highlights.title: Kledung, the easy start
highlights.body: Kledung is the favourite route: easy public transport, and local motorbike rides can take you and your gear to Pos 1.

stats.label: Ascent time
stats.note: Sandy upper slope slows you down

stats.label: Water to carry
stats.note: Springs only at the lower pos

stats.label: Sleeping bag rating
stats.note: Cold, windy nights near the top

packing.why: The upper slope is loose volcanic sand that gets into your boots.
On the sand it is two steps forward, one step back. Poles save your legs.
The summit is exposed to very strong wind and fog.
Springs are only on the lower pos. Carry all water for the upper section.

assessment.title: Sandy and tiring
assessment.body: Near the summit the trail is steep, slippery sand. Expect slow progress and sore legs.

assessment.title: Exposed summit
assessment.body: The top has no shelter. Wind can be extreme, so turn back if the weather turns.

assessment.title: Cold nights
assessment.body: Pack a sleeping bag rated to about 0°C and warm layers for the pre-dawn summit push.

slamet.tagline: The roof of Central Java: a long, remote climb on an active volcano.

highlights.title: Highest in Central Java
highlights.body: Slamet is the highest mountain in Central Java. It sits between five regencies: Brebes, Banyumas, Purbalingga, Tegal and Pemalang.

highlights.title: Bambangan, the main route
highlights.body: Bambangan is the best-known and best-managed route, with the shortest climb. It starts at about 1,510 m, some 90 minutes from Purwokerto.

highlights.title: A volcano that still breathes
highlights.body: Slamet has been at Level II (Waspada) since October 2023. PVMBG sets a no-go radius around the crater that changes with activity.

packing.why: Toxic gas pockets sit near the crater above Pos 4.
Extreme cold high on the mountain, and most people camp one night.
There is no water above the Samarantu spring at Pos 4.
Dense forest and a long exposed summit area mean you can get wet and chilled.

assessment.title: Check PVMBG first
assessment.body: Slamet is an active volcano. Only go when the status allows, and respect the crater no-go radius set by PVMBG.

assessment.title: Very long climb
assessment.body: Plan two days. The ascent takes 10-14 hours, and altitude sickness is possible near 3,400 m.

assessment.title: Loose volcanic top
assessment.body: Above Pos 4 (Samarantu) the ground is loose rock and sand, with gas pockets near the crater.

prau.tagline: An easy climb to a wide summit meadow with sunrise over Sindoro and Sumbing.

highlights.title: Sunrise between two volcanoes
highlights.body: From the summit ridge the sun rises behind Sindoro and Sumbing, often above a sea of clouds.

highlights.title: Camp on the meadow
highlights.body: Many hikers pitch a tent on the open summit and wait for sunrise the next morning.

highlights.title: Patak Banteng, the short way
highlights.body: Patak Banteng is the favourite and closest route to the top: about 3.9 km with 554 m of climbing.

stats.label: Summit elevation
stats.note: On the edge of the Dieng Plateau

stats.label: Night low
stats.note: Cold and windy on the open meadow

stats.label: Water to carry
stats.note: Buy water in Dieng before you start

The open meadow has no shelter from the wind.
There is no water on the trail. Buy it in Dieng first.
The grassland has little shade once the sun is up.

assessment.title: Gentle but uphill
assessment.body: The trail is short and steady uphill, with small rocks and red soil. Most beginners can manage it.

assessment.title: Slippery when wet
assessment.body: In the rainy season the red soil turns very slippery. Dry season hikes are much easier.

assessment.title: Cold is the challenge
assessment.body: The hardest part is a cold, windy night on the summit. Good layers and a warm bag solve most of it.

ungaran.tagline: Semarang's home mountain: tea gardens, forest and an easy summit.

highlights.title: Four ways up
highlights.body: Ungaran can be climbed from Basecamp Mawar, Candi Gedong Songo, Promasan and Perantunan. Mawar is the most popular.

highlights.title: Tea gardens at Promasan
highlights.body: Around 1,450 m the trail reaches Promasan hamlet, with springs, a camp area and wide green tea gardens.

highlights.title: 9th-century temples nearby
highlights.body: Candi Gedong Songo, a Hindu temple complex from the Medang Kingdom, sits on Ungaran's slopes at about 1,200 m.

packing.why: The trail gets slippery in the wet season and fog is common at the summit.
Springs are only low on the mountain. Carry your own for the top.
Some sections are steep and rocky, and slick after rain.

assessment.title: Beginner-friendly
assessment.body: No major danger points. It is a good first mountain if you can walk uphill for a few hours.

assessment.title: Some steep, rocky bits
assessment.body: Expect short steep and rocky sections. Take them slowly, especially when wet.

assessment.title: Fog at the top
assessment.body: The summit often clouds over. Stay on the marked path when visibility drops.

andong.tagline: A short beginner hike to a ridge with views of Merapi, Merbabu and more.

highlights.title: Mountains all around
highlights.body: From the top you can see Merapi, Merbabu, Sindoro, Sumbing, Prau, Ungaran and Telomoyo just by turning around.

highlights.title: Four little peaks
highlights.body: Andong has four peaks in a row from west to east. The highest is Andong peak itself.

highlights.title: Up one way, down another
highlights.body: A popular plan is to climb from Dusun Pendem (shorter, steeper) and come down via Sawit (longer, gentler). The two are about 700 m apart.

stats.label: Ascent time
stats.note: Short enough for a sunrise trip

packing.why: There is no water source on the trail. Carry your own.
The upper grassland is open and sunny once the sun is up.
The path gets slippery when wet, and the Pendem route is steep.

assessment.title: Easy for beginners
assessment.body: No major danger points. Most people reach the top in 2-3 hours.

assessment.title: Busy on weekends
assessment.body: Weekends get crowded, especially for sunrise. Go on a weekday for a quieter summit.

assessment.title: Watch the wet trail
assessment.body: After rain the path turns slippery. Take the gentler Sawit route down if unsure.

telomoyo.tagline: A quiet volcano between big peaks, with views over Rawa Pening lake.

highlights.title: Views over Rawa Pening
highlights.body: The summit looks out to Merapi, Merbabu, Sumbing and Ungaran, and down over Rawa Pening lake.

highlights.title: Hike it or ride it
highlights.body: A paved road runs almost to the top, so you can also go up by motorbike or jeep. Walkers can use the Arsal basecamp trail.

highlights.title: Paragliding launch
highlights.body: The summit area is a known take-off spot for paragliding and hang-gliding.

packing.why: There is no water on the trail. Carry your own.
The summit is windy, even on a clear day.
The path gets slippery when wet.

assessment.title: Easy and short
assessment.body: No major danger points. It is a relaxed beginner hike.

assessment.title: Share the summit
assessment.body: Because a road reaches the top, expect vehicles and visitors who did not walk up.

assessment.title: Wet and windy
assessment.body: Take care on slippery ground after rain, and bring a layer for the wind on top.

sikunir.tagline: A 30-minute walk from Java's highest village to a golden Dieng sunrise.

highlights.title: Java's highest village
highlights.body: The walk starts in Sembungan, known as the highest village in Java at about 2,350 m.

highlights.title: Named after turmeric
highlights.body: 'Sikunir' comes from the Javanese 'kunir', turmeric, for the yellow colour the sky turns at sunrise.

highlights.title: Sindoro at dawn
highlights.body: The hilltop gives clear views over the Dieng Plateau and Mount Sindoro as the sun comes up.

packing.why: Pre-dawn temperatures are around 0-5°C while you wait for sunrise.
You walk in the dark and the path has little lighting.
The farm path can be slippery.

assessment.title: Very easy walk
assessment.body: The climb takes 30-45 minutes on a farm path. No real danger points.

assessment.title: The cold is the hard part
assessment.body: You start around 3-4 AM in near-freezing air. Dress warmly and bring a light.

assessment.title: Dry season is clearer
assessment.body: Fog is less likely in the dry months, so sunrise views are more reliable.

gede.tagline: Rainforest, hot springs and an edelweiss meadow, about 70 km from Jakarta.

highlights.title: UNESCO Biosphere Reserve
highlights.body: Gede and Pangrango form a national park named a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 1977, about 70 km south of Jakarta.

highlights.title: Surya Kencana meadow
highlights.body: Alun-Alun Surya Kencana is a high savanna below the summit, covered in Javan edelweiss. It is protected, so look but do not pick.

highlights.title: Walk through hot water
highlights.body: On the Cibodas route the path crosses warm volcanic water flowing over rocks. Hikers hold a rope and walk slowly.

stats.label: Water to carry
stats.note: Cibodas route has springs along the way

packing.why: It is rainforest. The trail is slippery in the wet season and fog is common.
The summit is cold, especially at night and before dawn.
Help on slippery trail and on the hot-water crossing.
Most hikers start or finish in the dark, and fog can cut visibility on the upper trail.

assessment.title: Moderate, not technical
assessment.body: An intermediate climb. The Cibodas route is gentler, with many rest posts and a big camp at Kandang Badak (about 2,400 m).

assessment.title: Gas at the crater
assessment.body: Sulfur gas pockets sit around the crater. Keep to the rim path and do not linger in smelly hollows.

assessment.title: Busy on weekends
assessment.body: Permits fill fast on holidays and the summit can have queues. Weekdays are calmer.

pangrango.tagline: West Java's second-highest peak, with an edelweiss meadow just below the top.

highlights.title: Edelweiss at Mandalawangi
highlights.body: Alun-alun Mandalawangi is an alpine meadow less than 10 minutes' walk down from the summit. Its wide fields of edelweiss grow among the grass.

highlights.title: Second-highest in West Java
highlights.body: At 3,019 m, Pangrango stands second in West Java, after Ciremai. Its summit is called Mandalawangi.

highlights.title: Close to Jakarta
highlights.body: The mountain sits about 80 km south of Jakarta, inside Gunung Gede Pangrango National Park.

stats.label: Summit elevation
stats.note: Cold, wet cloud forest near the top

stats.label: Water per person

The ridge is cold, and fog and wet clothes make it colder.
Water is limited past Gede. Fill up at Kandang Badak and carry 3-4 L.

assessment.body: Between Gede and Pangrango the trail is easy to lose when fog rolls in. Stay together and check your GPS often.

assessment.body: The traverse takes 10-12 hours up and 7-9 hours down on a muddy, slippery trail. Fitness matters more than skill.

assessment.title: On your own up there

ciremai.tagline: The roof of West Java: a lone 3,078 m cone with a crater at the top.

highlights.title: Highest point in West Java
highlights.body: Ciremai is a symmetrical stratovolcano and the highest point in West Java, at 3,078 m. It rises southwest of Cirebon.

highlights.title: Crater at the summit
highlights.body: The summit holds a crater about 0.5 km wide. The last recorded eruption was in 1951.

highlights.title: History at Linggarjati
highlights.body: At the foot of the mountain, the Linggarjati museum marks the 1946 talks between Indonesia and the Netherlands.

packing.why: The summit area is cold, and most hikers camp on the mountain.
The ascent is steep and long. Poles save your knees on the way down.
Springs are only at Pos 1-2. You must carry all water above Pos 3.
Fog and cold are common on the upper slopes.

assessment.title: Relentless climbing
assessment.body: The trail climbs steeply for 8-10 hours with few flat breaks. Train your legs before you go.

assessment.title: Exposed above Pos 4
assessment.body: The upper sections and the crater rim are steep and exposed. Fog can roll in fast.

assessment.title: Plan your water
assessment.body: There is no water above Pos 3. Dehydration is a real risk on this climb.

papandayan.tagline: A dead forest, a steaming crater and an edelweiss meadow on one short trail.

highlights.title: Hutan Mati, the dead forest
highlights.body: The 2002 eruption burned the vegetation here. Dry, bare trees still stand upright on pale sulfur ground.

highlights.title: Tegal Alun edelweiss
highlights.body: About an hour's walk from Hutan Mati, Tegal Alun is a wide meadow full of edelweiss.

highlights.title: An active crater
highlights.body: Papandayan has four large summit craters. The youngest holds active fumarole fields that you walk past on the trail.

stats.label: Summit elevation
stats.note: Cold nights at the summit camp

packing.why: The trail passes active sulfur fumaroles. Gas levels change with the wind.
It gets cold at the summit camp at night.
Carry your own. Water is sold only at the basecamp.
Many hikers camp overnight near the Tegal Alun meadow.

assessment.title: Stay on the marked path
assessment.body: In the fumarole field, do not leave the path. Toxic gas can build up where the wind drops.

assessment.title: Easy on the legs

assessment.title: Cold after dark
assessment.body: Nights at camp are chilly. Bring warm layers even if the day feels mild.

salak.tagline: Deep rainforest next to Bogor, and one of Java's easiest places to get lost.

highlights.title: Kawah Ratu crater
highlights.body: Kawah Ratu is a field of small steaming craters at about 1,338 m, formed in the 1938 eruption. It sits 4.5 km along the Salak trail.

highlights.title: Java's big rainforest
highlights.body: Halimun Salak protects the largest remaining rainforest in Java. Javan leopards, Javan gibbons and Javan langurs live here.

highlights.title: A 2,211 m park icon
highlights.body: Salak is one of two main peaks in Mount Halimun Salak National Park, between Bogor and Sukabumi.

assessment.title: Navigation is the real test
assessment.body: The trail system is one of Java's most confusing, with many unmarked forks. Carry a GPS track and never walk alone.

assessment.title: Wet, steep ground
assessment.body: Expect mud, stone, roots and small river crossings. Good boots make a big difference.

assessment.title: Watch the rain
assessment.body: Heavy rain can cause flash floods in the ravines. Avoid the wet months and turn back if it pours.

cikuray.tagline: The tall cone above Garut, with sunrise views across West Java's volcanoes.

highlights.title: Top of the Priangan highlands
highlights.body: Cikuray is the highest peak in the Parahyangan/Priangan highlands, a dormant cone that dominates the land around Garut.

highlights.title: Views to many volcanoes
highlights.body: On a clear day the summit looks out to Ciremai, Guntur and Papandayan. Sunrise and sunset give the best views.

highlights.title: Start among the tea
highlights.body: From Pos Pemancar, the trail begins through tea plantations before entering the forest.

assessment.title: Steep upper forest

assessment.title: Long for its height
assessment.body: Plan for 6-8 hours up. Some fit hikers do it as a day hike by starting very early.

assessment.title: Wild boars about
assessment.body: Wild boars on the slopes are used to hikers. Keep food packed away at camp.

guntur.tagline: An active volcano near Garut whose 1847 lava reached the Cipanas hot springs.

highlights.title: 24 eruptions since 1690
highlights.body: Guntur has at least 24 recorded eruptions since 1690. The largest in historic times was in 1843.

highlights.title: Lava that reached Cipanas
highlights.body: The 1847 eruption sent lava flows to the Cipanas area, about 4 km from the summit. It has been quiet on the surface since.

highlights.title: Still alive below
highlights.body: Ongoing quakes under the volcano point to an active, melt-bearing magma system, despite no eruption since 1847.

stats.label: Summit elevation
stats.note: Part of a complex of overlapping volcanoes

stats.label: Last eruption
stats.note: Lava reached Cipanas, about 4 km away

stats.label: From Garut
stats.note: The complex lies about 10 km NW of the city

packing.why: Sulfur gas collects around the crater area.
Loose volcanic ground is hard on ankles, going up and coming down.
There is no water on the trail. Carry all you need.

assessment.title: Check if it's legal first
assessment.body: Guntur is a nature reserve (cagar alam). Officials say climbing has no permit, so routes may be closed at any time.

assessment.title: Check PVMBG alerts
assessment.body: Volcanic quakes rose in March 2026. Always check the alert level before you plan a trip.

assessment.title: Loose ground near the top
assessment.body: The crater area has unstable, loose volcanic terrain and gas. Keep to the known path.

burangrang.tagline: A short pine-forest climb on the rim of an ancient volcano near Bandung.

highlights.title: Remnant of old Mount Sunda
highlights.body: Burangrang, Tangkuban Perahu and Bukit Tunggul are what remain of ancient Mount Sunda after its caldera collapsed.

highlights.title: Pine forest start
highlights.body: From Legok Haji, the trail starts in gentle pine forest, then climbs over roots and steep ground to the top.

highlights.title: Waterfall on the way
highlights.body: Near Pos 1 a side path leads to Curug Cipalasari, a waterfall you can visit on the Legok Haji route.

packing.why: Dense fog and rain are common on the upper trail.
The trail is slippery, with roots and some steep sections.
There is no water source on the trail. Carry your own.

assessment.title: Steeper after Pos 1
assessment.body: The start is gentle, but from Pos 1 to Pos 2 the trail gets steep and rooty. Take your time.

assessment.title: Good first day hike
assessment.body: With a short route and phone signal close to Bandung, it suits hikers building experience.

assessment.title: Slippery when wet
assessment.body: Fog and rain make the roots and soil slick. Watch your footing on the way down.

kerinci.tagline: Sumatra's highest point and Southeast Asia's highest active volcano.

highlights.title: Highest volcano in the region
highlights.body: At 3,805 m, Kerinci is the highest point in Sumatra and the highest volcano in Indonesia and Southeast Asia.

highlights.title: World Heritage rainforest
highlights.body: Kerinci Seblat National Park is part of UNESCO's Tropical Rainforest Heritage of Sumatra site.

highlights.title: Tiger country
highlights.body: The park is one of the most important places in the world for Sumatran tiger conservation.

stats.label: Summit elevation
stats.note: Nights can drop to -10°C at the top

packing.why: Summit temperatures can drop to -10°C.
Leeches are common in the lower rainforest.
The last stream is near Shelter 1. Carry all water above it, 5-6 L.
The summit crater gives off volcanic gas.

assessment.title: An expedition, not a day hike
assessment.body: Plan 2-3 days. Hire a local guide: people have gone missing after trekking alone.

assessment.title: Hard summit push
assessment.body: From Shelter 3 the final climb is on steep volcanic sand and scree. Start early and turn back if gas is strong.

assessment.title: Altitude and cold
assessment.body: At 3,805 m, altitude sickness is possible. Go slowly and watch for headaches or nausea.

sibayak.tagline: A short sunrise hike to a steaming crater, with hot springs waiting below.

highlights.title: The 'King's Mountain'
highlights.body: Sibayak's name comes from the Karo Batak language and means 'King's Mountain'. It sits just outside Berastagi, about 70 km from Medan.

highlights.title: Steaming crater
highlights.body: At the top, fumaroles push out hot, sulfurous gas. The crater is just over an hour's walk from the nearest road.

highlights.title: Hot springs after
highlights.body: Natural hot springs lie about 5 km from the trailhead, a good place to rest tired legs.

stats.label: Ascent time
stats.note: Many start at 4 AM for sunrise

stats.label: Minimum age
stats.note: Younger hikers need a parent or guide

packing.why: The crater gives off sulfur gas.
The summit is cold and windy, especially before sunrise.
Most hikers start around 4 AM to catch the sunrise.
The climate is wet, and fog is common near the top.

assessment.title: Easy but not trivial
assessment.body: The hike is short and well-trodden. Slippery steps and fog are the main challenges.

assessment.title: Respect the vents
assessment.body: Do not step into fumarole holes. Steam vents can be dangerously hot and gas builds up in low spots.

assessment.title: Cold at dawn
assessment.body: Sunrise hikers face a cold, windy summit. Bring a warm layer even if Berastagi feels mild.

sinabung.tagline: Closed to climbers. An active volcano best seen from a safe distance.

highlights.title: Woke after 400 years
highlights.body: Sinabung was quiet for about 400 years before it erupted on 29 August 2010.

highlights.title: Thousands evacuated
highlights.body: Eruptions in August and September 2010 forced 26,137 people to leave their homes.

highlights.title: Years of activity
highlights.body: More eruptive periods followed: 2013-2018, 2019 and from August 2020.

stats.label: Summit elevation
stats.note: Do not climb: exclusion zone in force

assessment.body: The whole mountain is an exclusion zone. Pyroclastic flows, lahars and ash falls have killed people here.

assessment.title: Watch from afar
assessment.body: Viewpoints around Berastagi give a safe look at the volcano. Follow PVMBG and local guidance.

assessment.title: Ash can travel
assessment.body: Wind can carry ash to nearby towns. A mask helps if ash is falling where you are.

dempo.tagline: South Sumatra's highest volcano, climbed from the tea gardens above Pagar Alam.

highlights.title: Start in the tea gardens
highlights.body: The climb begins on gravel roads through a tea plantation. After 20-30 minutes you reach the forest edge, where the trail turns uphill.

highlights.title: Seven craters and a lake
highlights.body: Seven craters sit around the summit. A lake about 400 m wide lies at the north-west end of the crater complex.

highlights.title: A volcano that is still awake
highlights.body: Dempo is an active stratovolcano. It erupted on 7 April 2026, and the trail was closed until late May.

The summit is cold, and dense fog and rain are common.
Dense fog and limited rescue access make navigation harder.

assessment.title: Active crater
assessment.body: Gas and unstable ground at the crater are the main dangers. Check the PVMBG status before you go, as the trail closes after eruptions.

assessment.title: Long, remote day
assessment.body: Expect 6-8 hours up and 4-6 hours down. Rescue access is limited, so a local guide is recommended.

assessment.title: Cold and fog
assessment.body: The top is cold and often wrapped in fog. Bring layers and rain gear even in the dry season (May-September).

rinjani.tagline: Indonesia's second-highest volcano, with a crater lake and a young volcano inside.

highlights.title: A lake inside the crater
highlights.body: Segara Anak ('Child of the Sea') sits at about 2,000 m. Volcanic heat keeps the water just above 22°C, and pilgrims bring offerings to it.

highlights.title: A volcano within a volcano
highlights.body: Gunung Barujari, a small active cone, rises from the lake. It grew during a burst of activity in 1994-1995.

highlights.title: Hot springs by the lake
highlights.body: Hot springs near Segara Anak are a place to rest tired legs. Three of them hold spiritual meaning for local people.

stats.note: Wind can make it feel colder

The summit push starts around 2-3 AM in the dark.
The final climb is on loose volcanic scree.

assessment.title: Hard summit push
assessment.body: From Pelawangan you climb about 1,087 m in 3 hours on loose sand. It often feels like two steps up, one step back.

assessment.title: Cold nights
assessment.body: The crater-rim camp can fall to 7-8°C at night and the summit to 0-5°C. A warm sleeping bag matters.

assessment.title: Steep lake descent
assessment.body: The path down to Segara Anak is steep and slippery. Take it slowly, especially when tired.

agung.tagline: Bali's highest and holiest mountain, climbed at night for sunrise.

highlights.title: Bali's spiritual centre
highlights.body: Balinese people believe ancestral spirits dwell on Agung. Pura Besakih, the Mother Temple, and Pura Pasar Agung sit on its slopes.

highlights.title: Two routes, two temples
highlights.body: One trail starts at Pura Besakih, the other at Pura Pasar Agung. Both start in the middle of the night to reach the top for sunrise.

highlights.title: Highest point in Bali
highlights.body: At 3,031 m, Agung is the tallest peak on the island. Clouds often cover the view by late morning.

packing.why: The ascent is done at night to reach the top for sunrise.
The summit is very cold before dawn.
There is no water source on the trail.
Both trails start at temples; this is a sacred site.

assessment.title: Steep and unmarked up high
assessment.body: The upper third is very steep and loose, with no trail markers or protection. Go with a guide.

assessment.title: Active and sacred
assessment.body: Agung can close at short notice for volcanic activity or ceremonies. Check the PVMBG alert level the day before.

assessment.title: Night start, long day
assessment.body: You set off in the middle of the night. Plan for cold, darkness and a tiring descent on loose ground.

batur.tagline: Bali's easiest sunrise volcano, with a caldera lake below the summit.

highlights.title: A UNESCO Global Geopark
highlights.body: The Batur caldera is part of the UNESCO Global Geoparks network for its volcanic landscape.

highlights.title: Breakfast from the volcano
highlights.body: Steam vents near the top still cook the eggs served at sunrise. Lava fields from eruptions between 1804 and 2000 lie below.

highlights.title: Sunrise over the lake
highlights.body: Batur sits inside a double caldera beside a lake. At dawn the light spreads across the caldera and the water below.

assessment.body: About 2 hours up on a clear path. It is steep in places but safe if you stay on the trail.

assessment.title: Slippery way down
assessment.body: The descent on loose volcanic rock and the lava field crossing are where most slips happen. Go slowly.

assessment.title: Chilly at the top
assessment.body: People dressed for tropical Bali get cold while waiting for sunrise. A jacket makes the stop enjoyable.

tambora.tagline: The volcano behind the largest eruption in recorded history, and its huge caldera.

highlights.title: The 1815 eruption
highlights.body: Tambora's 1815 eruption was the most powerful in recorded history. It cut the peak from about 4,300 m to its current height.

highlights.title: A 6-7 km wide caldera
highlights.body: The eruption left a caldera 6-7 km across and 600-700 m deep. Hikers look down into it from the rim.

highlights.body: Day one crosses humid jungle with plenty of leeches. Near the top, plants thin out to ash and volcanic rock.

Remote area, dense forest navigation and no signal on the trail.

assessment.title: Remote and long
assessment.body: About 28 km round trip with no phone signal and limited rescue. A local guide is required.

assessment.title: Careful at the rim
assessment.body: The caldera rim has sheer drops and unstable edges. Keep well back from the edge.

assessment.title: Dry season only
assessment.body: Hike May-September. The trail is impassable in the wet season, and it can close for fire risk in the dry season.

inerie.tagline: A near-perfect volcanic cone above Bajawa and the Ngada villages of Flores.

highlights.title: A cone above Bena
highlights.body: Inerie rises over Bena, one of the best-preserved traditional villages in Flores, and looks out over the coast.

highlights.title: Sunrise behind Ebulobo
highlights.body: On a clear day the summit shows Bajawa, the Savu Sea and the sun rising behind Ebulobo, an active volcano.

highlights.title: Close to town
highlights.body: The trailhead at Watumeze village is about 30 minutes' drive from Bajawa.

assessment.body: No shade low down and hard wind up high. Start before dawn to avoid the midday heat.

assessment.title: Hard descent
assessment.body: Loose rock and small ravines make the way down slow and tiring. Leave energy for it.

latimojong.tagline: The roof of Sulawesi: a multi-day climb through moss forest to Rante Mario.

highlights.body: Rante Mario is the highest point in Sulawesi and one of Indonesia's Seven Summits.

highlights.title: Deep moss forest
